notes: All 40 manifest files read in full; no partners. Scope removed (ACTION-REVIEW-SEC-004): none of the assigned files was skipped. Examined but not raised: (1) the policy gate trusts the runner and verifier code of the branch under check — a gated repo running go run ./cmd/acdsl, or a target's bin/acdsl and bin/verifiers/*, can be edited to neuter CheckPolicy itself, so adding verifier sources to policySurface would not close it; this is architectural (trusted-runner placement), not a fix in this diff. (2) peek /healthz identity in cmd/configserver/main.go can be spoofed by another local user, but that user already reaches the unauthenticated configserver on the shared loopback, so the spoof grants nothing new. (3) Probe side effect: shell.Run returns combined stdout+stderr, so a refname-ambiguity warning lands in GitMergeBase's parsed sha; the result is a fail-closed exit 2, not a bypass. Cross-chunk: install.sh (other chunk) renders __PEEK_HOME_ARGS__ raw into the plist XML — not verifiable here. Known-ledger matches skipped: security-MAJ-1-r2, security-MAJ-2-r1, security-MAJ-9-r1, correctness-MAJ-9-r1, correctness-MAJ-51-r1, correctness-MAJ-52-r1. Probe repo left at artifacts/round-1/scratch/sec-l2-probe.

findings.fix: Resolve policy-base candidates as fully qualified refs (refs/remotes/origin/HEAD, refs/remotes/origin/main, refs/heads/main, refs/heads/master; a set base_ref qualified via git rev-parse --symbolic-full-name and rejected when it lands under refs/tags/) before git merge-base, so a tag can never stand in for the base branch.
findings.claim: policyBase passes the bare names origin/HEAD, origin/main, main, master to git merge-base, and git resolves a bare name through refs/tags/ before refs/heads/ and refs/remotes/; in a gated or strict repo with an empty base_ref and no refs/remotes/origin/main (no origin remote, or an origin without that ref), a branch runs one allowlisted command, `git tag origin/main`, and the policy base becomes its own HEAD: every committed rule removal and self-management-surface edit on the branch then diffs to nothing and CheckPolicy returns zero diagnostics, and basePolicy reads the branch's own committed policy.json, so the branch can also commit mode free.
findings.evidence: Re-read policy.go:195-219 (candidates list, GitMergeBase(ctx, root, candidate), first resolving candidate wins, baseName TrimPrefix origin/ -> isBoundary true for any other branch) and git.go:69-75 (git merge-base HEAD <ref>, unqualified). Probe with the head's prebuilt bin/acdsl in a scratch repo under artifacts/round-1/scratch/sec-l2-probe: main commits policy {mode gated, editable_scopes [GOLANG]}, registry {gofmt}, rules ACDSL-GOLANG-100 + ACDSL-PLAN-100; branch work commits removal of ACDSL-PLAN-100 and an added registry entry. `acdsl check` exit 1 with two ACDSL-POLICY diagnostics (registry.json differs; ACDSL-PLAN-100 removed outside the editable scopes). After `git tag origin/main` (no other change): `acdsl check` exit 0, 'acdsl: 1 rule(s) OK'. Cost: one command, zero file changes, permanent until the tag is deleted. Shadowing a name that also exists as a branch or remote ref (tag main beside refs/heads/main) instead makes git print a refname-ambiguous warning into shell.Run's combined output and the check fails closed (exit 2), so the bypass needs the shadowed candidate to have no real ref — the no-origin / no-origin-symref state. No repo runs gated today (smine policy mode is free; dist targets receive dist_mode gated), so exposure is set to eventually. Distinct from known correctness-MAJ-9-r1 (base_ref edited in the working policy.json) and correctness-MAJ-52-r1 (origin/ prefix stripping): this needs no file edit and the base_ref fix does not close it.
